This page contains an incomplete list of books I have read or listened to, inspired by the edX course _Behavioural Economics in Action_ that I took in Fall 2020. Most of these books have something to do with economics (which was not entirely by choice) and/or data analytics. This list is ongoing and is being updated periodically.

The list is ordered alphabetically by book titles.

- _101 Theory Drive_: A Neuroscientist's Quest for Memory, by Terry McDermott [Link](https://www.amazon.com/101-Theory-Drive-Neuroscientists-Memory/dp/0375425381/)
- _2030_: How Today's Biggest Trends Will Collide and Reshape the Future of Everything, by Mauro F. Guillen [Link](https://www.amazon.com/2030-Biggest-Collide-Reshape-Everything/dp/1250268192/)
- _21 Lessons for the 21st Century_, by Yuval Noah Harari [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Lessons-21st-Century-Yuval-Harari/dp/0525512195/)
- _A Short History of Nearly Everything_, by Bill Bryson [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Short-History-Nearly-Everything/dp/076790818X/)
- _Alan Turing_: The Enigma, by Andrew Hodges [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Alan-Turing-Enigma-Andrew-Hodges/dp/0802775802/)
- _Beginners_: The Joy and Transformative Power of Lifelong Learning, by Tom Vanderbilt [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Beginners-Transformative-Power-Lifelong-Learning/dp/1524732168/)
- _Bezonomics_: How Amazon Is Changing Our Lives and What the World's Best Companies Are Learning from It, by Brian Dumaine [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Bezonomics-Amazon-Changing-Companies-Learning/dp/1982113634/)
- _Breaking Boundaries_: The Science Behind our Planet, by Johan Rockstrom and Owen Gaffney [Link](https://www.amazon.com/Breaking-Boundaries-Johan-Rockstrom/dp/0744028132/)
